articleTitle: Robust Adaptive Controller Design for DC-DC SEPIC Converter In Photo Voltaic Application
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a controller based on robust adaptive control applied to a non-minimum phase Sepic<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> converter by PWM<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> method. The mathematical modeling, used to display the frequency response characteristic, is presented by the average model of the converter. The proposed system is a fourth order non-minimum phase system which is approximated to a second order system based on frequency characteristics of the system. By considering noise, nonlinear properties, disturbances, unmodeled dynamics, and variation of injected voltage to the system, some limitations are discussed in designing of the controller. In this case, conventional controllers are not so useful, therefore the indirect self-tuning adaptive controller has been proposed which consists of two parts: identification and control signal production, moreover robust adaptive controller is designed based on estimator improvement. Finally, the simulations are performed by using MATLAB-Simulink and the effectiveness of the controller will be shown.

articleTitle: Adaptive PID Control Design for Longitudinal Velocity Control of Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: An adaptive cruise control system is designed to control the longitudinal velocity of a vehicle based on the PID model reference adaptive control. The proposed technique seeks for an admissible throttle and braking policies that cause the longitudinal velocity of the vehicle tracks a desired behavior in the existence of realistic situations such as various road conditions and aerodynamic effects. Because of the presence of nonlinearity and time-varying conditions, the controller is modified with robust update laws to guarantee the boundedness of signals. The effectiveness of the proposed theoretical achievements is validated via high-fidelity CarSim software package by considering adverse path conditions and aerodynamic force in the opposite direction of the longitudinal velocity.

articleTitle: ANN-Based Frequency and Tie-Line Power Control in Interconnected Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: Microgrids can operate in three different possible modes, including grid-connected, islanded and the interconnected operation modes. One of the big challenges in the interconnected microgrids is frequency and tie-line power control because of the nonlinearity behavior of the interconnected microgrids. Thus an adaptive controller is needed for solving this problem. In response to this challenge, in the present paper, an artificial neural network controller is presented. The control methodology is applied to two-AC interconnected microgrids considering a simplified frequency response model. The effectiveness of the proposed controller is examined by simulation. The simulation results show that in different conditions, artificial neural network controllers can operate better than the conventional proportional-integral controllers.

articleTitle: Observer-based Sensor Fault Detection in Islanded AC Microgrids Using Online Recursive Estimation
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: Performance and security of power systems are threatened with different classes of faults. Each fault considering its place and severity has a detrimental effect on system stability and performance. This fact makes fault detection and control essential. Although the system may suffer from output degradation in this case, appropriate control methodologies take place to mitigate the adverse effects of faults and maintain stability. This paper investigates fault detection problem, in a well-established islanded AC microgrid benchmark, which its applications have been substantially developed thanks to microgrids’ superiority over traditional power systems. The proposed sensor fault detection approach is based on online recursive model estimation and observer-based residual generation. Using the estimated model, linear Kalman filters are designed to provide the residual signals, based on which a sequential change detection unit will decide whether the system is in normal operation mode or a fault has occurred.

articleTitle: Improve the Frequency Identification in SSVEP based BCI Systems with Moving Windows Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: Most processing methods used in SSVEP-based BCI systems use fixed time windows for frequency identification. Due to the variable nature of the EEG signal timing, the use of fixed time windows is not appropriate. In this paper, a new algorithm for floating windows is proposed and evaluated with CCA and LASSO frequency detection methods. The results show that the use of the moving window algorithm for LASSO and CCA methods improves the maximum percentage of frequency identification accuracy by 3.76% and 6.25% respectively. Furthermore, this method decreases the frequency identification time to 0.55 seconds and 0.79 seconds compared to the fixed window algorithm. Advantages such as being able to apply to all frequency recognition methods, increasing the frequency identification accuracy at a certain time of processing compared to fixed windows, adding unlabeled state and adaptability based on system requirements make this algorithm one of the best candidates for SSVEP-based BCI systems.

articleTitle: Sensor Fault Detection in a Distributed Power System via Decentralized Kalman Filters
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: The problem of fault detection (FD) of large-scale systems has been considered in this paper. The proposed FD approach employs decentralized Kalman observers for simultaneous estimation of states and detecting sensor faults in the presence of noises in the model and sensory measurements. Then, decentralized model predictive controllers (MPC) has been designed based on the estimation of states. Also, the residual signals will be constructed via Kalman filters. The proposed FD scheme does not rely on the availability of full state measurements. The residual evaluation function is derived from a change detection algorithm called cumulative sum (CUSUM). The performance of the proposed FD approach is evaluated through simulations performed for a case study, namely FD of a distributed power system.

articleTitle: Fault Tolerant Kalman Filter-Based Distributed Predictive Control in Power systems Under Governor Malfunction
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: Power systems are disposed to frequent faults, which may occur in any of its components, such as generating units, transformers, transmission network and/or loads. Governors, depending on type, suffer from the same faults that would be expected to find in any mechanical, hydraulic or electrical device or system. Determination of governor faults effects on system behavior and system stability was of special interest in this work. Here a distributed Kalman filter (KF) algorithm along with a distributed model predictive control (MPC) is proposed to maintain system performance while governor fault takes place. Distributed KF-based MPC estimates and control. The estimation of governor state and comparing with its real value results in fault detection where two control approaches are proposed to help system keep its stability and performance. The proposed control strategy is used in a demanding two-area power network.

articleTitle: Adaptive Neural Observer-Based Nonsingular Terminal Sliding Mode Controller Design for a Class of Nonlinear Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: Solving the problem of control, stability, and maneuvering of an Air-Cushion Vehicle (ACV), as a nonlinear system, is a key challenge in amphibious vehicles. Nonlinearity, external disturbances, internal uncertainties, and unmodeled dynamics are the main difficulties that an ACV is faced with in the maneuver control. In this paper, a methodology is derived from designing an observer-based controller for an ACV. An adaptive Neural Networks (NN) observer with guaranteed stability is designed for the nonlinear dynamics of an ACV, which is controlled by the nonsingular terminal sliding mode controller. It is assumed that states of the system are unknown, while the system is observable. The main merits of the proposed method are the Lyapunov stability of the closed-loop system, the convergence of the tracking and observer errors to zero, and robustness against uncertainties. Simulation results demonstrate the performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Metro Traffic Regulation by Considering the Effect of Transfer Stations
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: This paper proposes appropriate regulation by considering the effect of the transfer stations in the metro traffic system. The inherent instability is one of the most important characteristics of these types of systems because any delay grows in time and propagates to the other trains.Since passengers play a major role in delay transmission, transferring passengers between the trains of different metro lines leads to transfer the delay from one line to another one in transfer stations. In this paper, the synchronization departure time of trains from transfer stations considers as a constraint to delay recovery in metro networks.

articleTitle: State Estimation Of a Quantum Cavity Driven by single-photon
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: The cavity is a fundamental ingredient of quantum optical systems. This paper concerns the behavior of a quantum cavity driven by non-classical field in single-photon state. To this end, the number operator has been opted to reveal the number of photons inside the cavity. Then, the quantum filtering equations have been employed to derive a stochastic master equation for the cavity which is driven by single-photon and is observed by either Homodyne or photon-counting detector. Finally, the state of the cavity has been estimated by the derived equations, and the results have been compared with the conventional master equation.

articleTitle: Glucose Control In Diabetic Patients Considering Daily Real Life Factors
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: Diabetes Mellitus (DM), is recognized as one of the most critical health challenges of the 21<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> century. It can affect almost every part of the body and leads to health problems and complications such as heart, kidney, eye, dental, and nerve disease. Therefore, it is needed to manage blood glucose levels by insulin injection that can be done either by syringe injection or insulin pump. The insulin pump is the most recent method of insulin injection, which transfers certain amounts of insulin to the body in regular and certain time distances.In this paper, the goal is to control one of the most complete models of glucose-insulin metabolism in Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM) patients. This nonlinear and time-varying model considers the T1D patients body in real daily life. Important factors such as meals, snacks, physical activity and exercise, fatigue, stress, and insulin sensitivity (SI) drift are modeled. While most articles treat meals and exercise as disturbances, in this paper, these factors are included in the considered mathematical model.The feedback linearization technique is exploited to design a suitable nonlinear controller by considering the uncertainties and time-varying functions. The performance of the proposed controller is verified through simulation tests. It is clear from the simulation results that the controller is successful in keeping the blood sugar level at the desired level.

articleTitle: Distributed Actuator Fault Detection and Estimation for Linear Multi Agent Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: This paper proposes a new distributed actuator fault detection and estimation scheme for linear multi agent systems. Information exchange between the agents is described by an undirected graph. The considered faults are time-varying and they have abrupt characteristic. Also, state variables of the system are not available. The proposed distributed fault detection algorithm designs a diagnostic estimator based on the relative local information to monitor the status of each agent, generate residual signal and detect fault. After that, an adaptive fault estimation module is activated to estimate the detected fault. The proposed scheme is formulated as a linear matrix inequality problem and its stability analysis is proved. Finally, to verify the effectiveness of the proposed structure, some simulation results are presented.

articleTitle: Analytical Approach to Nonlinear Behavior Study of an Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: Permanent Magnet Direct Current (PMDC) motors have great application potentials in Electric Vehicles (EVs) industry, due to their advantages, such as no need for the field excitation arrangement, no input power consumption for the excitation, and having lower costs for low power rating applications. To analyze the nonlinear behavior of the EV equipped with the PMDC motor, the electromechanical equations related to a typical model of the PMDC motor are derived, and the electrical equivalent circuit related to the mechanical equations is presented in this paper. Homotopy Perturbation Method (HPM) and Variational Iteration Method (VIM) as the two analytical techniques are applied to solve the evolution equations. The performance of the PMDC motor that is concerned with the nonlinear parameters (viscous friction, torque, and inertia) is evaluated. In addition, the accuracy of the two analytical techniques is compared with the numerical solution. The results confirm the applicability of the two analytical techniques to analyze the nonlinear behavior of the system.

articleTitle: Soft Sensor Design for Distillation Columns Using Wavelets and Gaussian Process Regression
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: Process variables whose measurements using the available equipment seem impossible or difficult are estimated inferentially by some computer programs called "soft sensors". In this paper, a novel soft sensor algorithm is designed to estimate the concentration of benzene, the bottom product of a distillation column. Wavelet denoising and Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) are utilized in the soft sensor design. Comparing to the other soft sensor designs, this model benefits from a high accuracy and less modeling complexity. The simulation results show promising robustness against the measurement noise.

articleTitle: Polytopic-LPV Robust Control of Power Systems Connected to Renewable Energy Sourcess
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: This paper deals with a robust polytopic-linear parameter varying (LPV)-based controller to regulate DC bus voltage in a direct current (DC) islanded microgrid. The considered DC MG involves photovoltaic (PV) cells, wind turbines (WTs), and storage units. The nonlinear state-space representation of the overall DC MG system is obtained and the equivalent polytopic-LPV model is derived. Then, the objective of the polytopic-LPV-based controller is to I) extract maximum power point (MPP) from PV array, II) extract maximum power from wind energy in the WT, and III) regulate the voltage of the DC bus. The controller design conditions are derived in terms of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs), which simplify designing a nonlinear controller for the high-order nonlinear DC MG system by using numerical LMI toolbox solver. Finally, numerical simulations are done to show the effectiveness of the suggested robust polytopic-LPV controller.

articleTitle: A 3-PRS Parallel Robot Control Based on Fuzzy-PID Controller
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: In this paper, a new Type-II Fuzzy-PID based approach is proposed to control a 3-PRS parallel robot. 3-PRS parallel robots are very common in industrial applications due to their high precision. In addition, according to the unique kinematic characteristics of these kinds of robots, they are capable of avoiding the singularity at the zenith angle during the tracking. The two inputs of the Fuzzy System (FS) are the error and its changes. The proposed controller applies the best control signal to the robot system by determining the PID coefficients. The simulation results confirm that a PID controller tuned by the Type-II Fuzzy system is an effective method to control these kinds of robots. The performance comparison of the Type-I and Type-II Fuzzy systems indicates the superiority of the Type-II Fuzzy system.

articleTitle: Robust stabilization of discrete-time switched systems with state delay and parametric uncertainty via model predictive control approach
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: This paper is devoted to investigating the robust stabilization of a class of nonlinear switched systems with state delay and uncertainties under arbitrary switching signals. For this purpose, a robust model predictive control (RMPC) method is developed for online optimization of an infinite horizon cost function. Sufficient conditions in terms of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs) are derived to guarantee the robust stability of the closed-loop system. To reduce the computational load and the conservatism of the stability analysis, parametric uncertainties are considered. Numerical and practical examples are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A New Type-II Fuzzy System for Flexible-Joint Robot Arm Control
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: In this paper, an Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) based on the Interval Gaussian Type-II Fuzzy sets in the antecedent part and Gaussian Type-I Fuzzy sets as coefficients of a linear combination of the input variables in the consequent part is presented. The capability of the proposed control method to function approximation and dynamical system identification is investigated. An adaptive learning rate based on the Backpropagation method with guaranteed convergence is employed for parameter learning. Finally, the proposed method is applied to control a flexible-joint robot arm. The simulation results show the robustness and effectiveness of the proposed control method. The proposed control method is also compared with the conventional ANFIS method.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Control of an Uncertain Robot Manipulator with Input Constraint
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: In this paper, an adaptive fuzzy dynamic surface control scheme is proposed for an uncertain n-link robot manipulator with input saturation. The fuzzy logic system is used to approximate the uncertain dynamics of the robotic manipulator. Also, a hyperbolic tangent function-based saturation model and mean value theorem are employed to design the proposed scheme based on the dynamic surface control approach. Stability analysis of the proposed approach guarantees that all signals of the closed-loop system are semi-globally uniformly ultimately bounded. Simulation results on an uncertain 2-joint robot manipulator verify the ability of the proposed approach to deal with both the saturation nonlinearity and uncertain dynamics.

articleTitle: Simultaneously Parameter Identification and Measurement-Noise Covariance estimation of a Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: This paper proposes the online parameters identification of semi-empirical models of Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell (PEMFC). The covariance of unknown measurement noise is also estimated simultaneously. The actual data are fed to Kalman (for linear-in-parameters models) or extended Kalman filter (for nonlinear ones) which have been adapted for parameter identification. These filters suffer from the fact that the noise of the measurements is unknown. In order to tackle this conundrum, the measurement-noise is simultaneously estimated, and the estimation is used in the filters. The ultimate consequence of estimating measurement-noise is error reduction which has been demonstrated by simulation results.

articleTitle: Optimal State Estimation of Air Handling Unit System without Humidity Sensor using Unscented Kalman Filter
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: One of the main Heating, Ventilating and Air Conditioning (HVAC) devices which is located on the path of coolers or boilers is the air handling unit (AHU). AHU is a device which provides healthy and clean air by providing proper temperature and humidity. There are a lot of nonlinearities and couplings among variables of this system which makes design of the control system and state estimation, an attractive and challenging problem. In this paper, purpose is to design an unscented Kalman filter (UKF) based on scaled unscented transformation (UT) for state estimation of the AHU system controlled via a linear quadratic regulator (LQR). This filter employs UT and statistical characteristics to calculate more terms of the Taylor extension and increase estimation accuracy. Using UT preserving nonlinear characteristics of the AHU without linearization, offers an optimal estimation with proper speed and accuracy which can be used for any kind of state feedback controller. Simulation results demonstrate proper performance of the proposed method compared to extended kalman filter (EKF).

articleTitle: Lyapunov Exponent based Stability Assessment of Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: Lyapunov exponent (LE) is a mathematical-based analysis tool to assess the stability of dynamical systems and this can be done by two approaches: model-free approach and model-based approach. In this paper, the model-based approach is employed as an indicator of stability for the stability analysis of power systems. The maximum Lyapunov exponent (MLE) is used to investigate the effects of increasing load on the stability and stability region of the power system where the positive (negative) value of MLE means instability (stability). Also, LEs are used to assess the effect of the presence of renewable energy on the stability of power systems. Simulation results are presented on the single-machine system and fixed-speed induction generator (FSIG) wind turbine system which show the disadvantages of increasing load or adding renewable energy sources on the system stability.

articleTitle: Robust H2 and H∞ controller design for DC position motor control under uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: DC motors are often used in a variety of industrial applications. These motors are easily controllable and their position can be adjusted with low cost. However, one of the problems that hampers the motor control, despite the proper initial design, is the change of control system parameters. Indeed, each control system should be robust for a pre-defined range of internal and external changes. In this paper, an attempt is made to discuss the mathematical model of the motor and the associated nonlinear factors. Afterwards, a robust control scheme, which considers torque as an external perturbation signal and nonlinear dynamics in the motor, is proposed to control position of DC. To this end, H2 and H∞ methods are combined.

articleTitle: Design of a Nonlinear Model-based Predictive Controller for a Wind Turbine Based on PMSG Using an Augmented Extended Kalman Filter
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: In this paper, a novel nonlinear model-based predictive controller without speed/position sensors is designed for control of a wind turbine permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) and grid. Here, both grid and generator sides are controlled via a predictive mechanism including an optimization subject to nonlinear constraints of current and voltage amplitudes as well as the harmonic distortion magnitude of currents. To have a sensorless design, a Kalman filter is also designed. First, an extended Kalman filter (EKF) is used to estimate the speed and then an augmented extended Kalman filter (AEKF) is designed to estimate the flux without the need to add complex equations. The simulation results show an acceptable performance of the proposed method despite the changes in the reference speed and disturbance.

articleTitle: High-Performance Robust Grid-Connected Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: This paper studies a novel robust voltage regulator to manipulate a boost direct current/alternating current (DC/AC) inverter in grid-connected power systems. It is assumed the AC side feeds unknown loads and the characteristics of the network line and the grid have uncertainties. Based on the active and reactive powers of the connected grid, the references for the currents of the gird are designed. Also, to simplify the controller design procedure the abc to dq0 change of coordinate is used. Moreover, to reduce the CO2 emissions of the conventional diesel motors/generators fuel cells are deployed as the main source. However, the challenge of stabilizing the voltages and currents of the AC MG is handled by a robust μ-synthesis based controller. To evaluate the performance of the designed controller, several scenarios with constant and time-varying references and different uncertainties are performed.

articleTitle: Connected Vehicles Are Now Abolishing the Conventional Traffic Measuring Tools
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: Advanced traffic control and management strategies rely either on the real-time measurements or on the estimates of the macroscopic traffic variables. While for many years loop detectors have been the widespread sensing tools, capable of measuring flow and occupancy, connected vehicle data has emerged as a new data source for traffic measuring and estimation. In this paper, it is demonstrated that the loop detectors in urban networks can be eliminated and the necessary measurements can be retrieved from connected vehicle data based on the proposed modeling approach. The proposed methodology is tested and validated with promising results.

articleTitle: A Controller Design based on Iterative Learning method and Model Predictive Control for a nonlinear process system
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: This paper proposes a controller using model predictive control and iterative learning control algorithm for a class of nonlinear process. A predictive control model computes system outputs, and accurate prediction is the desired purpose. Model predictive controller relies on dynamic models of a system, linear empirical models are mostly derived from system identification. In order to control a system accurately, an accurate model is needed. These control purposes can be achievable by using iterative learning algorithm. This type of modeling is applied for the first time in this paper for a nonlinear process. Iterative learning algorithm improves the performance of the processes that perform the same motion or operation repeatedly. This proposed method is capable of improving the accuracy of a model and the robustness of this method in presence of repetitive disturbance. The rejection of repetitive disturbance and deterministic modeling error which caused from repetitive disturbances by iterative learning algorithm has been proved. The proposed method is used for controlling liquid level in two-tank. The simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Robust Tracking Control of Boiler-Turbine Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel robust output feedback controller to regulate the output electric power of a nonlinear boiler-turbine system. The suggested approach is based on the robust mixed-µ-synthesis and the uncertain linear representation of the boiler-turbine system. Based on the real data, the system is linearized around a practical operating point and the practical ranges of the uncertainty terms are chosen. Besides the output electric power, the pressure and the water level are also regulated to be in the desired range. The developed approach offers an outline procedure to design a linear output controller, which is robust against the boiler-turbine uncertainties and external disturbances. To assess the robust performance of the designed controller, several scenarios with constant and time-varying references and different disturbance inputs are given.

articleTitle: Design a New Intelligent Control for a Class of Nonlinear Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: This paper presents a new method based on computational intelligence for precise control of a class of nonlinear systems. In this method, the Radial Basis Function Neural Networks (RBFNN) is used to approximate the uncertain functions in the system dynamics. In addition, a constraint is considered on the input. The Backstepping method is used for improving the overall accuracy of the control process. To evaluate the performance of the proposed method, a single-link robot arm with nonlinear dynamics and input saturation constraint is investigated. The simulation results show the performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Chaotic Time Series Forecasting using Emotional Learning-Based Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: This paper has investigated a new model based on the brain emotional learning to forecast chaotic series. The proposed model is based on the Moren model which is a model of the emotional part of the brain of mammals. In this paper, we have extended the Moren model based on the actual inputs to the thalamus of mammalian brain, i.e., the number of entries to the thalamus is considered to be more than one. A better performance in chaotic time series forecasting has been achieved in simulations. The results show that in comparison with other methods such as neural network based models and fuzzy neural models, the proposed model has less MSE in both short-term and long-term forecasting for the chaotic time series.

articleTitle: Smith Predictor Based Sliding Mode Control for Torsional Vibration Control of Drillstring with Input Delay
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: This paper presents a smith predictor based sliding mode controller to eliminate torsional vibrations in oil well drillstrings. The drillstring model is considered as a torsional pendulum with four degrees-of-freedom. The control objective of the system is tracking desired angular velocity without stick-slip oscillations. The main purpose of this paper is to design a controller dealing with both input delay and uncertainty in the nonlinear bit-rock interaction appropriately. For robustness in the presence of parameter uncertainty in drillstring model a sliding mode controller is proposed. However, smith predictive control method is used to deal with input delay. Asymptotic stability of the system and reference angular velocity tracking is proved by the Lyapunov method. Simulation results confirm that, the designed controller is robust in the presence of parametric uncertainties while preventing torsional vibrations in the drillstring, under input delay.

articleTitle: Optimal gait design for the lower extremity exoskeleton (Exoped)
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: Assistive robots have been grown in recent years and joints’ moving pattern is one of the important issues in these robots. The predefined trajectory for the robot brings some stability difficulties for the users. This paper introduces a systematic way to produce an optimal gait for the controller of the lower extremity exoskeleton. This optimal gait producing strategy releases us from the exhausting procedure of walking pattern capture in different paces which requires various devices and motion analysis lab. A feedback-controlled system is defined which enables us to change walking parameters during steps with a smooth walking pattern which is of vital importance for the patients in these kinds of robots. This goal has been achieved by solving an optimal control problem, and the cost function of this optimization problem is obtained thorough walking limitations. Implementation on the Exoped robot verifies the performance of the proposed walking trajectory planning method in this paper.

articleTitle: Industrial Boiler-turbine-generator Process Control Using State Dependent Riccati Equation Technique
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: In this paper, to control the drum pressure, the generated power, and the fluid density in the industrial boiler-turbine-generator unit a tracking controller is designed. Due to the nonlinear model of this process and some constraints in its inputs, the proposed controller is designed based on the State Dependent Riccati Equation (SDRE) method which is a powerful approach in this area. In this system, that is a multiple inputs, multiple outputs (MIMO) system, three control valves (CV) - the fuel CV, the feed water CV, and the steam flow CV - are used as the actuators of the system in order to control three outputs of the system - the drum pressure, the generated power, and the fluid density - respectively. To evaluate the designed controller, it is applied to the system and the performance of the system is assessed for several operating points. The simulation results demonstrate that by means of the designed controller the system has a very good performance.

articleTitle: Accuracy Improvement of GPS/INS Navigation System Using Extended Kalman Filter
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: Inertial navigation is a method for determining position and orientation of a vehicle, which operates according to Newton’s laws of motion. Due to continual increase of output error because of measurement noise, bias, misalignment and so on, one may need one or more additional navigation systems to improve accuracy in long-term navigation. In this paper, the error compensation based on GPS/INS data fusion algorithm is studied. Then, by designing a DSP processor-based hardware, GPS and INS data are recorded and GPS/INS data fusion algorithm is implemented. Results indicate that the accuracy of the positioning is improved and position, velocity, and orientation errors are confined to a limited range.

articleTitle: Fault Tolerant of Ship Roll Motion Using the Control Allocation Approach
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: This paper presents a fault-tolerant ship roll motion control using the control allocation approach (CA) in the presence of actuator faults. An control allocation method is applied based on the optimized l<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> norm of the control signal. The practical actuator constraints are also considered. An active fin is used that is commanded by a PID controller. The active fin actuator is most effective at high speed. Simulation results are used to show the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Estimation of V47/660kW Wind Turbine State and Fault Detection with Extended Kalman Filter
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: In this paper we study Fault Detection of Wind Turbine. The wind turbine in this study is V47/660kW that is installed in Manjil wind farm in Gilan province. In this article, various parts of the wind turbine, including the pitch angle actuator, rotor speed sensor and generator speed sensor, have been investigated. In fact, fault detection has been done for these three turbine components. For this purpose, the Extended Kalman Filter has been used. Extended kalman filter is one of the most efficient estimators to be used in fault detection process and estimation of wind turbine state. Fault detection is done according to the residual generation. The residual is the difference between the state/output of actual system and the state/output of estimated system using the extended kalman filter. After the production of the residual, we study the occurrence and non-occurrence of fault in the wind turbine. We use Math work Laboratory software in this paper.

articleTitle: Fault Detection and Control of Time-Delay Systems: A Disturbance Observer Approach
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: This paper deals with the fault detection, diagnosis and control problems of time delay systems by designing a disturbance observer (DOB). In proposed method, the DOB estimates the changes occurred as an input disturbance. In fact, the DOB is implemented as a residual generator for the system. Subsequently, the estimated changes can be used to compensate the effect of faults and plant alterations directly. In this method, the estimated disturbances can be used for the FDI purpose and the final system would be fault tolerant, without the need to have all other faults isolable and identifiable. It provides a simple, low cost and effective fault detection and isolation method which can be applied to more practical systems. The applicability and effectiveness of the proposed method is illustrated by the simulations provided for an industrial water pressure control system which is supposed to be subject to faults.

articleTitle: Analyzing the effect of output measurements interval and impulses distance of an impulsive observer on the control system of HIV
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: Extended state-dependent Riccati equation (ESDRE) control system based on a state-dependent impulsive observer is developed for HIV, as a nonlinear time-delay system. The state-dependent impulsive observer takes measured outputs at discrete moments and uses those to estimate state of the system, continuously. The estimated values of state variables are used in control ESDRE control strategy. The impulses- distance is chosen with respect to the patient physical limitations. A time-varying Lyapunov function and comparison system theory of impulsive differential equation systems are used to prove the stability of this observer, since the observer and the controller are independent, another Lyapunov function can be used to guaranty the asymptotic stability of the closed-loop control system. Simulation results are provided to show the efficiency of the output measurements- interval and impulses distance of an impulsive observer on the control and estimation of the HIV time-delay model.

articleTitle: Notice of Violation of IEEE Publication Principles: Fault Tolerant Control Scheme Using Adaptive Sliding Mode Control Allocation
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract:
Notice of Violation of IEEE Publication Principles

"Fault Tolerant Control Scheme Using Adaptive Sliding Mode Control Allocation,"
by N. Abbasi, A. K. Sedigh, M. Naderi and S. R. Jafari,
in the Proceedings of the 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA), October 2019

After careful and considered review of the content and authorship of this paper by a duly constituted expert committee, this paper has been found to be in violation of IEEE’s Publication Principles.

This paper contains portions of text from the paper(s) cited below. A credit notice is used, but due to the absence of quotation marks or offset text, copied material is not clearly referenced or specifically identified.

"Fault Tolerant Control for Over-actuated Systems: An Adaptive Correction Approach"
by S. S. Tohidi, Y. Yildiz and I. Kolmanovsky,
in the Proceedings of the American Control Conference (ACC), July 2016, pp. 2530-2535


This paper presents an adaptive control allocation for the over-actuated systems in order to improve set-point of the flight systems. Also, a sliding mode controller incorporates control allocation is employed to control the outer loop. The sliding mode control allocation methodology is able to manage faults/failures using the effectiveness matrix of the actuators, without reconfiguring the controller. To show the effectiveness of the proposed approach, a admire with redundant actuators is simulated.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Active Vibration Control and Energy Regeneration Study in Tall Structures
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: The problem of vibration control in tall buildings using an active pendulum as the vibration absorber using fuzzy control is considered. Fuzzy logical rule base is presented and the performance of the fuzzy controller is verified by simulation tests. The amount of energy loss in the actuator is also calculated and the possibility of the energy regeneration from the structure is investigated. Active control together with an energy regeneration is also investigated. Simulation results show the effectiveness of the fuzzy active control when the energy regeneration part is also active.

articleTitle: Neural Networks Adaptive DSC Design of Nonlinear Systems in the Presence of Input Saturation and External Disturbance
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: This paper offers a robust adaptive control based dynamic surface control for uncertain nonlinear systems in the presence of actuator saturation and external disturbance. Radial Basis Function Neural Networks are used for approximating uncertain nonlinearities. Using dynamic surface control technique, the problem of explosion of complexity caused by differentiating the virtual controllers during the recursive procedures in the conventional backstepping method is avoided. The proposed controller guarantees uniformly ultimately boundedness of the closed loop system. The effectiveness of the proposed method is illustrated with a simulation example.

articleTitle: Design, Implementation and Control of a Multilevel Cascade Inverter for AC Drive Application with Improved Low Speed Operation
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: AC electric drives today are widely used in small and large industries to start up and control single-phase and three-phase AC motors. During the start-up period, these drives should limit the current magnitude in addition to maintaining torque. It must also be able to control the speed of the motor in a steady state with the electrical and mechanical parameters that meet the standards at the same time. In this paper, some of the standards for adjustable speed AC drives are first reviewed. Then the design and implementation process of a low voltage/ medium power multilevel inverter is briefly explained. Some electrical/ mechanical constrains that an AC motor drive should satisfy are extracted from the standard. Then a hybrid control algorithm is proposed for low speed and high speed operation which is simple and efficient. Simulation and experimental results on a 400 V three phase 5 hp induction motor is presented to evaluate the design.

articleTitle: Output Voltage Control of Inverters Using SDRE Tracking and LQT Controllers
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: This paper presents novel nonlinear and linear control methods for output voltage control of a three-phase inverter. For implementation of these optimal controllers, the nonlinear and linear models of the system including LC filter have been derived. Moreover, analysis of the system under the State-Dependent Riccati Equation (SDRE) and Linear Quadratic Tracking (LQT) as the nonlinear and linear optimal controllers has been done and comparison between performance of them is investigated in MATLAB environment.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Fuzzy Cerebellar Model Articulation Controller for Synchronization of Chaotic Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: This paper aims to propose an adaptive fuzzy cerebellar model articulation controller (FCMAC) for synchronization of two chaotic systems in the presence of uncertainties and external disturbance. The proposed controller is comprised of parametric fuzzy rules. The antecedent part of every rule remain steady, while the subsequent part is renewed with every time step by establishing adaptation laws. These adaptation laws are derived by the Lyapunov synthesis approach and guarantee the closed-loop system's stability. Simplicity, low memory demand and rapid control satisfy the practical usage of the adaptive FCMAC. Furthermore, adaptation laws can overcome lack of human experts knowledge about the chaotic plant. Eventually, simulations for synchronization of two Duffing-Holmes chaotic systems reveal that a satisfactory tracking performance can be achieved by using the proposed control system.

articleTitle: Optimal Feedforward Design for a Class of Non-minimum Phase Integrating Systems with Time Delay
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: In this paper, an optimal feedforward controller is addressed for a class of non-minimum phase integrating systems with time delay. Firstly, the drawbacks of the classical feedforward design for such systems including being non-realizable, are highlighted and then, a technique is presented to cope with such difficulties. By decomposing plant to two individual parts, a new configuration is suggested that converts the non-minimum system to an augmented minimum phase one. The resulting integrating system is then handled by a suitable form of the feedforward controller. To tune the controller in an optimal fashion, an algorithm is presented that seeks for a parameter that minimizes the ISE index. The effectiveness of the proposed control design is validated by a numerical example.

articleTitle: Variable Structure Control of Spacecraft based on Nonlinear Sliding Surface
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: Attitude measurement sensors' (sun-sensor, magnetometer and etc.) accuracy play a significant role in the performance of the spacecraft attitude control system (ACS). On the other hand, the continuous use of attitude sensors is not possible due to their intrinsic limitations. So achieving the suitable performance of the ACS in the absence of the attitude sensor's data is an important problem that is addressed in this paper. The abovementioned problem is more challenging in the case of agile and high-angle non-smooth maneuvers. In this regard, a new approach for designing a variable structure control (VSC) based on the nonlinear sliding surface is presented to deal with high nonlinear effects of non-smooth maneuvers in the absence of attitude sensors. Accordingly, a new term is added to the standard conventional sliding mode controller (SMC), turning it into a practical solution for the proposed problem. This term also gives more flexibility to the controller designer to adjust the gains of the control law, which may lead to (i)faster time-responses of the spacecraft without an increase in overshoot, and (ii)also a lower steady-state error.

articleTitle: A Safe Optimal Third-Order Decentralized Consensus of Uni-directional Heterogeneous Vehicular Platoons with Communication and Parasitic Delays
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: In this paper, a safe optimal decentralized consensus protocol is presented to assure internal and string stability and safety of heterogeneous vehicular platoons. Since time delay is an inherent characteristic of physical actuators, communication and parasitic delays are involved in system modeling and stability analysis. A prevalent third-order model is employed to describe the longitudinal motion of each vehicle. The communication topology of platoon is assumed to be unidirectional and the constant time headway policy is employed to adjust the inter-vehicle spacing. By using the relative position and velocity information with respect to preceding vehicle, a linear control is designed for each following vehicle. By calculating the closed-loop dynamics of each vehicle, internal and string stability and safety are analyzed in presence of time delays. To optimize the control parameters, the imperialist competitive algorithm (ICA) is employed. Several simulation results are provided to show the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Decentralized Estimator-based Secondary Voltage and Reactive Power Control of an Islanded Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: A decentralized secondary control approach is proposed to compensate voltage deviations and to improve reactive power sharing accuracy in islanded microgrids. A state observer according to Kalman filter theory is designed based on a reduced order small-signal model to estimate reactive power and system voltages through local measurements without using communication system. An optimal tuning algorithm is used to tune PI controller in voltage control loop and a regularly tuned PI controller is used for compensating reactive power error. The effectiveness of the proposed control strategy is verified by the simulation of a microgrid test system in SIMULINK/ Simscape toolbox.

articleTitle: Robust Stabilization of Affine Fuzzy Large-Scale Systems Using Decentralized Controller
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: This paper treats robust controller design for affine fuzzy large-scale systems (AFLSS) composed of Takagi-Sugeno-Kang type fuzzy subsystems with offset terms, disturbances, uncertainties, and interconnections. A decentralized nonlinear state feedback controllers are developed for stabilization of the overall AFLSS in terms of some sufficient conditions with low computational effort and free gains. A numerical example is given to illustrate the feasibility of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Cascade Terminal Sliding Mode Control of a Deployable Cable Driven Robot
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: Most control systems used for cable-driven parallel manipulators employ a simple inner control loop for controlling the driving force of the actuators. By this means the effects of some nonlinear uncertainties of the actuator and power transmission systems are significantly reduced, and in turn, this helps the outer user-specified position control loop to perform more accurately. However, this positive impact on performance relies on non achievable assumptions that the inner control loop is fast and accurate enough, and its dynamics can be totally ignored. The main contribution of this paper is to analyze the stability of the system as a whole, considering both inner and outer loop controllers. The outer loop controller proposed in here is a finite time robust sliding mode whose stability is analyzed through the Lyapunov direct method. A deployable cable-driven parallel robot, as the case study, is also considered in this paper, which is characterized by several intrinsic kinematic and dynamic uncertainties. Finally, the performance and effectiveness of the proposed robust controller is evaluated through some simulations and experiments in order to verify the effectiveness and the characteristics of the cascade controller structure in practice.

articleTitle: Robust H∞ Observer-based Sliding Mode Control for Discrete 2D Systems with Parametric Uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: In this paper, the robust observer-based H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> control is investigated using sliding mode control (SMC) for class of uncertain 2D systems represented by Modified Fornasini Marchesini (MFM) state-space model. At first, using the sliding mode control method and defining suitable 2D sliding surfaces based on estimated states, control law is designed such that insures the reachability of sliding surfaces. Afterwards, sufficient conditions are obtained to guarantee satisfying the H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> performance level of the closed-loop system for all bounded parameter uncertainties. Conditions are expressed in terms of solvable linear matrix inequality (LMI). Finally, a numerical example illustrated to verify the proposed method validation and efficiency.

articleTitle: Robust Fixed-order Dynamic Output Feedback Controller Design for Delayed Vehicle Active Suspension System with Polytopic Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: In this paper, a fixed-order procedure is presented utilizing convex optimization and linear matrix inequalities (LMIs) to control a quarter car uncertain active suspension system. Our purpose is to design a low-order robust controller that keeps the desired design specifications besides the simplicity of the implementation. In our model, the system is influenced by the non-linear disturbance of the road surface, and the polytopic uncertainty model for state matrices of the system is utilized to cover the uncertainties of the model and the delay caused by the dynamic of the system. In this paper, a specific form of a positive definite matrix is used to overcome the complexity of rank minimization constraints. The proposed controller is considered with the most general state-space representation of linear systems which can be resulted by solving appropriate LMI constraints utilizing available efficient solving methods. Our proposed controller benefits from the dynamic property, independency of all individual states of the system, being of arbitrary order, and robustness against model uncertainty simultaneously. Eventually, a simulation example is presented to illustrate the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed method and obtained results for different orders that are compared with each other and also with that of a similar full-order method.

articleTitle: Data-driven MIMO discrete-time predictive model-free adaptive integral terminal sliding mode controller design for robotic manipulators driven by pneumatic artificial muscles
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: In this paper, a data-driven multi-input multi-output discrete-time predictive model-free adaptive integral terminal sliding mode controller is proposed for the robotic manipulators driven by pneumatic artificial muscles with unknown models and external disturbances. First, using the concept of compact-form dynamic linearization technique, dynamics of the robotic manipulator are represented in discrete-time linear data-model form. Second, a time-delay based estimation algorithm along with an adaptive law is investigated to estimate external disturbances and pseudo-Jacobian matrix, respectively. Eventually, the proposed controller is derived based on a data-driven discrete-time integral terminal sliding function and by utilizing the concept of model-predictive controllers. The simulation results obviously clarify the efficacy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Robust Fault Tolerant Position Tracking Control for a Quadrotor UAV in Presence of Actuator Faults
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: In this paper, a robust fault tolerant controller is designed for an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) quadrotor against actuator faults in presence of external disturbances. First, nonlinear dynamic model of the quadrotor is considered as a Linear Parameter Varying (LPV) system in presence of the disturbances and actuator faults. Then, a robust fault tolerant control scheme is proposed by using adaptive estimation of the actuator faults for position tracking problem. For this end, the control input is designed as a summation of a normal control signal in the non-faulty conditions and an adaptive control signal in presence of the actuator faults which makes the tracking error asymptotically stable. Moreover, the H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> approach is adopted for robustness against the disturbances. The controller parameters can be obtained by solving a set of Linear Matrix Inequalities (LMIs). Simulation results are conducted to illustrate the effectiveness of the designed methodology.

articleTitle: Time Delay Controller Design for Dynamic Positioning of ROVs based on Position and Acceleration Measurements
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: In this paper, a control system is designed for dynamic positioning (DP) of an ROV with unknown dynamics, subject to disturbances using passive arm and inertial measurement unit (IMU). The proposed control system is composed of a nonlinear PD-type controller and time delay estimation (TDE) for estimating unknown dynamics and external disturbances. TDE is evaluated on DP of an ROV based on different sensors and numerical methods, namely, IMU sensor, Doppler velocity log, passive arm, a combination of passive arm and IMU, and numerical differentiation or integration of sensor data. To make the investigations more detailed and comprehensive, the effect of sensor noise, bias and integration drift are taken into account. Moreover, the performance of proposed control system is evaluated under different environmental conditions. Simulations show that the proposed method has superior performance compared to other control systems in terms of positioning accuracy and smoothness of control signal.

articleTitle: Design of a Suboptimal Controller based on Riccati Equation and State-dependent Impulsive Observer for a Robotic Manipulator
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: In this paper, Riccati equation and state-dependent impulsive observer (SDIO) are combined to design a controller for the nonlinear dynamical system of a robotic manipulator. A state-dependent Riccati equation-based controller is similar to optimal linear quadratic regulator where its Riccati equation employs pseudo linearization. Pseudo-linearization is a technique to represent systems with a structure similar to a linear system while preserving all characteristics of the original nonlinear system. It is stronger than the linearization technique via Jacobin method and does not need to change the operating point. Here it is shown that, the impulsive observer is able to estimate system states even if they are not transmitted from the sensors with a regular sampling rate. Via the proposed design, the stability of the closed loop system is analyzed using comparison principle which results in less conservative stability criteria. Applying pseudo linearization technique to the system and combining the Riccati equation controller and SDIO, suboptimal observer based control is obtained for the nonlinear manipulator systems especially when the system output is not accessible at all moments. The simulation results indicate the performance and efficiency of the proposed method in controlling the system.

articleTitle: Unscented Kalman Filter in Gas pipeline leakage magnitude estimation and localization
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: A model-based real-time transient modeling estimation process is proposed in a gas transmission line with the purpose of leak detection. The objective of this paper is aimed at determining the effectiveness of filtering techniques in leak detection and localization in a pipeline network through a synthetic pipe simulation. A model for a straight pipeline without any branch has been derived from Momentum and continuity equations and discretized based on the method of characteristics. In the next step by assuming proper boundary conditions, state-space representation of the system has been developed and stability and observability conditions have been explored. The unscented Kalman Filter has been selected as a nonlinear state observer. Simulations have been done in OLGA and PVTsim as multiphase flow simulators. The pressure measurements at the discrete points have been used as input to the state estimation algorithm. Finally, by defining different scenarios the effect of leak magnitude, location and time duration on the performance of the proposed method has been evaluated.

articleTitle: Exponential synchronization of a complex dynamical network with piecewise-homogeneous Markovian jump structure and coupling delay
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: In this paper, exponential synchronization problem is studied for a complex dynamical network (CDN) with a class of Markovian jump structure with coupling-time delay. The CDN under consideration has a piecewise-Markovian jump structure with piecewise-constant transition rates (TRs). First piecewise-homogeneous Markovian process is modeled by two Markov chains then, the synchronization problem of the CDN is inspected by constructing Lyapunov-Krasovskii function with Markov dependent matrices. Ultimately, the controller gain matrices for guaranteeing the synchronization problem in terms of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs) are derived. A CDN with a Chua circuit dynamic for each node is given as a numerical example to show the effectiveness of the theoretical results.

articleTitle: Distributed Robust Finite-time Non-linear Consensus Protocol for High-order Multi-agent Systems via Coupled Sliding Mode Control
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: This paper proposes a robust finite-time distributed tracking control problems for n-order non-linear multi-agent systems with a virtual leader in the presence of bounded disturbances and model uncertainties. The proposed algorithm is based on coupled n-order non-linear terminal sliding mode control which ensures the convergence of the agent's states to the virtual leader. The task is achieved in finite time by exploiting only local information. Thanks to the proposed non-singular terminal sliding mode control function, the derivatives of terms with fractional powers could not appear in the control law. Thus the control singularities could be avoided. Furthermore, the proposed terminal sliding mode control removes the chattering phenomenon by using a low-pass filter. Finally, numerical simulations are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed solution.

articleTitle: On adaptive chaos control and synchronization of a novel fractional-order financial system
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: This work mainly focuses on the dynamical behavior analysis of an uncertain novel 3D incommensurate fractional-order financial system including its chaos control and synchronization. Stability conditions of the equilibrium points and phase diagrams for this system are provided. Adopting the largest Lyapunov exponent criteria, it is found that the system yields chaos at the lowest fractional order of 2.15. Next, in order to globally stabilize and synchronize the chaotic fractional financial model with unknown parameters, an adaptive control technique is developed. Numerical simulations are used to illustrate the effectiveness of the presented adaptive controller.

articleTitle: Fieldbus Physical Layer Simulation Using HSPICE
publicationTitle: 2019 6th International Conference on Control, Instrumentation and Automation (ICCIA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel electrical modeling of a fieldbus physical layer. The main objective is to model a Fieldbus Physical Layer to allow a practical and flexible way to collect and analyze the different kinds of physical layer structure signaling and data. The fieldbus physical layer is a bidirectional low frequency and power transmission line with several nodes which allows the fieldbus signal to travel in a network between nodes and circulates the data stream. The proposed model is created based on transmission line modeling concept and has been simulated using HSpice. The performance of the proposed scheme is evaluated in comparison with real environment signal and compliance with the physical layer standard. The results verify the simulation performance as well as the model competency.
